definitions.title: Linearization (Tangent Line Approximation)
definitions.statement: If f is differentiable at x = a, the approximating function L(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x - a) is the linearization of f at a. The approximation f(x) approx L(x) is the standard linear approximation.
definitions.explanation: Replaces complicated non-linear functions with their tangent line locally around a.
definitions.keyTakeaway: L(x) is the tangent line equation used as a local estimator for f(x).

definitions.title: Differentials and Propagated Error
definitions.statement: Let y = f(x) be differentiable. The differential dx is an independent variable (the increment Delta x); the differential dy is defined by dy = f'(x) dx.
definitions.explanation: dy represents the change along the tangent line, which approximates the true change Delta y along the curve.
definitions.keyTakeaway: dy = f'(x)dx estimates the true change Delta y.
